purpose: Adopt explicit eye-specific relative rays from the CUDA tracker without mislabeling them as metric world geometry.

activities.label: preserve two eye rays and fail closed on unreliable relative geometry

queries.question: Can the existing CUDA provider expose two eye-specific relative rays without collapsing them into an average or claiming metric geometry?

assumptions: The existing eye-specific yaw and pitch convention can define a camera-aligned relative direction.
Image-normalized eye centres are useful as a relative baseline but not as metric eye separation.
A future metric stage will require independent camera intrinsics, eye depth and head pose.
The target is generated by VIZZ and is not inferred from the mouse.
kill_tests: Binocular disagreement above 45 degrees returns UNKNOWN.
Relative proxy output cannot be reported as metres or world pose.
No camera, network, screen mutation or raw video is used by the contract.
unknowns: Real webcam stability of the two rays under head motion, distance changes and glasses.
Whether the current angle convention remains stable after independent camera calibration.
The metric eye depth and monitor pose needed for physical multi-monitor geometry.
